hypotheses.title: PB125 Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: PB125, a combination of carnosol, withaferin A and luteolin, extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect results from the combined action of its three phytochemical components on cellular stress pathways.
hypotheses.rationale: The three constituents activate endogenous antioxidant and anti-inflammatory defenses that decline with age. Sustained activation of these pathways should slow the accumulation of molecular damage and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: PB125-treated mice will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of Mus musculus to PB125 or vehicle from midlife onward, maintain identical housing and diet, and follow all animals until natural death with blinded lifespan analysis.

hypotheses.title: Methylene Blue Shortens Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Methylene blue shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Chronic exposure to the compound imposes a net physiological cost that outweighs any beneficial effects.
hypotheses.rationale: Methylene blue is a redox-active agent that can perturb electron transport and cellular redox balance when administered chronically. Sustained redox disruption accelerates accumulation of oxidative damage and shortens survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Methylene blue-treated mice will show a statistically significant decrease in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of Mus musculus to methylene blue or vehicle from midlife onward, maintain identical conditions, and follow all animals until natural death with blinded lifespan analysis.

hypotheses.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Alpha-lipoic acid extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect is mediated by improved mitochondrial function and enhanced antioxidant capacity across tissues.
hypotheses.rationale: Alpha-lipoic acid is a mitochondrial cofactor and versatile antioxidant that supports energy metabolism and recycles other cellular antioxidants. Preserving mitochondrial integrity should slow age-related decline and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Alpha-lipoic acid-treated mice will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of Mus musculus to alpha-lipoic acid or vehicle from midlife onward, maintain identical conditions, and follow all animals until natural death with blinded lifespan analysis.

hypotheses.title: Acarbose Accelerates Ageing in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Acarbose accelerates ageing in Mus musculus. Chronic interference with carbohydrate absorption imposes metabolic stress that hastens age-related decline.
hypotheses.rationale: Acarbose blocks intestinal carbohydrate digestion, altering nutrient sensing and gut function. Chronic disruption of nutrient availability and microbiome balance can elevate stress signaling and accelerate the ageing process.
hypotheses.prediction: Acarbose-treated mice will show accelerated onset of age-related phenotypes and a statistically significant decrease in lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of Mus musculus to acarbose or vehicle from midlife onward, track age-related physiological markers and survival, and follow all animals until natural death with blinded analysis.

hypotheses.title: Anterior Hypothalamus Extract Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: Anterior hypothalamus extract extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect is mediated by factors in the extract that modulate neuroendocrine regulation of ageing.
hypotheses.rationale: The hypothalamus governs neuroendocrine signaling that influences growth, metabolism and systemic ageing. Supplying hypothalamic factors could restore youthful regulatory signaling and slow whole-organism decline.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving anterior hypothalamus extract will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of Mus musculus to anterior hypothalamus extract or vehicle from midlife onward, maintain identical conditions, and follow all animals until natural death with blinded lifespan analysis.

hypotheses.title: TM5441 Extends Lifespan in Mice
hypotheses.claim: TM5441, an inhibitor of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect is mediated by reduced PAI-1 activity and improved tissue homeostasis.
hypotheses.rationale: PAI-1 rises with age and promotes fibrosis, inflammation and cellular senescence. Pharmacological inhibition of PAI-1 should preserve tissue function and slow age-related decline.
hypotheses.prediction: TM5441-treated mice will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of Mus musculus to TM5441 or vehicle from midlife onward, maintain identical conditions, and follow all animals until natural death with blinded lifespan analysis.

hypotheses.title: Methylene Blue Extends Lifespan via Complex IV Restoration
hypotheses.claim: Methylene blue extends lifespan in Mus musculus by restoring mitochondrial complex IV activity in aged neurons. The lifespan benefit depends specifically on this neuronal mitochondrial mechanism.
hypotheses.rationale: Complex IV activity declines in aged neurons, limiting electron transport and energy production. Methylene blue can act as an alternative electron carrier, bypassing impaired steps and restoring neuronal bioenergetic capacity.
hypotheses.prediction: Methylene blue-treated aged mice will show restored neuronal complex IV activity together with a statistically significant lifespan increase relative to controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat aged Mus musculus with methylene blue or vehicle, measure complex IV activity in isolated neurons across brain regions, and compare survival between groups with blinded lifespan analysis.
